viewings.review: The acting by Washington and Crowe is very good. The story is intriguing, but it does move slowly, especially in the beginning. Some of the scenes do feel somewhat repetitive, especially the scenes of the drugs being distributed. Denzel’s ability to switch from quiet to charming to angry is what make the movie most interesting, the best example being when he smashes the guys head in the piano.

This movie, from a stylistic perspective, is maybe one of the most beautiful movies I’ve ever seen. Every single shot and frame feels deliberate. The colors feels soft and mellow, which combined with the music essentially creates a movie that feels like a painting. The acting is truly great, with all the performances feeling grounded and real. However, this film really has minimal that actually happens in the grand scheme of things. So you have to be comfortable with a movie that moves slowly.

Wow! What a plot! This might be one of the most interesting movies I’ve ever watched. The acting here is top notch, with the subtle performances of Hanks being captivating. All of the characters have a great chemistry. Some scenes are truly great to watch. From the Mouseville and the sudden squishing, to the last execution, the dialogue and acting make it hard to look away. The only thing is that they don’t really imply how Coffey ended up in the spot to be framed for the murder, which is a little annoying thread, but still very good. Michael Clark Duncan is huge

A great feel good movie. It’s like if Scent of a Woman, Good Will Hunting, and catcher in the rye had a baby. The scenery, lighting and music make for a very beautiful atmosphere for the film. Paul Giamattis performance was great. You feel the covering up of his reclusiveness with his intelligence. I found Dominic Sessa’s performance super interesting. While he plays a wise-kid, which tend to be very mature, Sessa allows for moments of childlike behavior to slip in, reminding us he’s not adult. From him jumping and dislocating his shoulder, to his “I’ll go pack line”, he’s not a typical, “I know more than all the adults characters.”. Da’vines performance also served as a good backbone for the story. Her quiet arc of accepting her son’s passing was something that really was a great side plot and made the character quite interesting. This is a feel good movie in every sense of the word. 8.5/10

A very gripping movie. Denzel Washington and tom hanks performances are top notch. I feel like the facial performances of both actors really sold the meaning and drama the most. The opera scene was hauntingly chilling. The ending montage was very sweet. The movie does take a bit to get going though.

There’s something about the pacing of this (and most Wes Anderson movies) where every scene feels important and easy to watch. The story in this one is very simple, and therefore very easy to digest. All of the voice acting is top notch. One thing is, It is a little confusing to determine if the dogs/humans can understand each other with the headpiece. The subtle humor of the movie is great, with little jokes catching me off guard. The fakeouts (the incineration; and the last fight) had me on the edge of my seat
A fun, turn-your-brain-off, heist movie. George Clooney is very captivating and fun to watch. The movie has great twists at the end, especially the SWAT and fake bank twist (this really got me). 7.5

This movie is like watching a long car crash. It’s hard to watch at times, but yet you’re glued to it. Brendan Fraser’s performance is amazing. His meek performance while surrounded by louder personalities makes for an interesting dynamic. Sadie sink does a good job, especially towards the end. I like that it’s somewhat ambiguous if her act towards the missionary was meant to do harm or good. The scene with Thomas showing Charlie the bible and reading it was really gripping, and the last scene was the best. This movie is sad, and at times, very gross, but it’s captivating. Be warned, you probably will not want to eat for like a day or 2 after watching this. 7.5

This movie is amazing. The movie flies by considering its length. The camerawork of the opening battle scene makes it feel frenetic, adding to the tension. Tom Hanks’ performance is interesting, as most military characters are very strong-willed and tough, whereas he’s more refrained; which goes in with the interesting twist that he’s a teacher. The calm before the storm with the song in French really added to the film and gave a nice breather yet you feel a small bit of tension. The soldier that was spared returning at the end was top notch, and the very end is a tear jerker

viewings.film: butch cassidy and the sundance kid|1969
viewings.review: Fun movie. The beginning is a little. The strong suit is Paul Newman and Rob Redfords acting and more specifically the dynamic between the 2 is really good. The scene with jumping into the river was really funny, in particular. The writing is quite funny. Though it doesn’t really feel like there’s an end goal or mission, so it’s hard to fully connect to or root towards.

This was a great movie that any one can enjoy. Ryan Gosling’s performance was fun and enjoyable. The plots very simple in a good way. The visuals are beautiful and the highlight of the film when paired with the score. The action scenes at the very end were very gripping. The leaking bit towards the end really came as a shock. I do wish they spent a bit more time on the learning of the communication, because it starts with the numbers and somehow they can communicate very well. Overall, a fun movie for the family. 8.5/10

This is like John Wick in WW2 with way less talking. Some of the actions scenes were unique, like the landmine scene, but most of the action was just ok. It felt a bit repetitive of: confrontation with nazis, gory injury, heal himself, repeat.

This movie might have some of the best performances I have seen in a movie hands down. All of the acting was so gripping. It is hard to look away. The pacing is perfect. The first 20 minutes are a little slow, but that’s a minor critique. The scene where Judith does not recognize the dead brother and Will slowly realizes he’s dead. Also, the ending performance is of course memorizing. I really like use of color, specifically Agnes red dress fading in color throughout, and the pit mirroring the stages was amazing. 9.5/10

A pretty funny movie. Nicholas cage’s acting was definitely more understated than usual, but still good. I particularly enjoyed Holly Hunter and John Goodman. I think the humor is pretty enjoyable, with the chase scene in particular being quite funny. There’s also some interesting camera work. It’s very silly and campy. 6.5/10

A very engrossing movie. From the beautiful imagery and the soundtrack (honestly might be a top 10), it’s very easy to get lost in the movie. There is a lot going on and to absorb, but the story is interesting. A very cute movie. 7.6/10

Once you get past the horrible cgi, and some very cheesy writing in some moments, you get a really fun adventure movie. Theres a lot of good jokes, like “Abdul, Mohammad, Bob”, “stay here while I get help”, etc.. All of the characters are fun and engaging, and Brendan Fraser’s charming adventurer is fun to watch. There’s movie doesn’t take it self seriously, and makes it a very pleasurable experience.

I was excited to watch this movie as I think both main actors are very good, but something just did not click. First, I think locking the kid in the closet seems on par with the planning of the shooting, so that made it feel less weighty at first (until they heavily focused on it). I think this movie portrays overthinking very well, and is definitely the highlight of the film. The movie is just basically one straight line of uneasiness and tension, with very little to oscillate, making the impactful moments, like the cheating and the reveal of it at the wedding, feel less impactful/uncomfortable, since you have that feeling throughout the whole movie. I think Robert Pattinson has some pretty decent range and plays awkward and uncomfortable well. I feel like Zendaya really doesn’t have a lot of range here, mostly playing reserved and holding back tears. I feel like the ending was also quite predictable

This movie feels very poetic. From the language, to the scenery, to the music, it has this very light tone. The chemistry between the characters is the star of the movie. It feels like you’re sitting in on a real couple. I think the way their eye contact (or lack of) and their body language really sell the beginning stages of a relationship/ the nervous energy. I think Ethan Hawkes mannerisms (little half smiles, hand fiddling, etc) really make the character feel real. I think the scene in the restaurant where they’re pretending to be on phone calls was definitely my favorite scene. A very sweet movie. 8.5/10

If Before Sunrise is the youngest child with hope and ambition, Before sunset is the depressed teen going through puberty. Though their chemistry is back almost immediately, the movie starts fairly bleak with their conversations of life and politics and it takes really until they board the boat to pick up. They also talk about sex a lot in this film, which is fine, but feels almost… repetitive? The highlight of the film was the scene in the car, where the subtle mannerisms and the acting from Delpy really shines. It feels like she is more of the main character in this film. I feel like the fade to black at the end is somewhat unsatisfying though. Overall, the chemistry and writing of the first one is back, but a bit desaturated, which makes sense for the characters. Not bad, but definitely prefer the first. 6.5/10

The last of the Before series really shows off the dynamics of Jesse and Celine’s relationship and really shows Ethan Hawkes and Julie Delpys connection. Like the second one, this one takes a bit to get going, but once they get to the hotel, the movie really becomes hard to look away. The back and forth, the small interjections of minor details (6 v 6:30) really make the argument feel real. I think the fact that they aren’t married, and it’s a small details that’s glanced over is an interesting take. The characters feel worn out, not in a bad way, but in a real way, like they’ve lived lives. I think the end, while the most weighted, has the hopefulness of the first one. This one does feel the most “big budget” out of the 3, which takes away a bit of the charm that the first (and partially the second) had, but it’s still good. 7.5/10

This might be my personal favorite Al Pacino role so far. His acting in this erratic, passionate, stressed, and every other emotion in between. This movie is basically 90% Pacino acting, and it’s great. The shouting matches on the streets are some of my favorites, and the back to back phone calls with Leon and his wife Angie were among the top. The pacing is very good, keeping me hooked the whole time, and it has a good blend of comedy, action, drama, suspense, and more. This movie is really just some top notch acting. 8/10

Very silly and campy. If you were to have a mental checklist of a James Bond movie, this would tick all the boxes. Fun gadgets, cool cars, bond hitting on every woman with a pulse, lasers. I think the beginning and end are ok, but the middle (from the laser scene to the middle of Kentucky) is the best part of the movie. Also, Pussy Galore is the craziest name in a movie of all time. 6.5/10

This movie really fits the epic nature of the odyssey. This feels like an epic in every sense: grand, loud, intense. The acting from everyone is great, Matt Damon’s Odysseus was great and I think tom holland got to show more range as his son. I think the movie does take a little bit to get going, but once they hit the scene with the cyclops, it really gets going from there and doesn’t stop. That cyclops scene is tense the whole way through, the Trojan horse and invasion scene feels epic, the witch scene is super hard to watch. The sound design with the ear wax was top notch and super unique! Almost every scene feels like one you can point to as the best. An epic film in every sense of the word. 8.5/10

DUCK TITTIES! This movie has everything you could ever ask for. Duck puns, duck boobs, and what else do you need? The villain is stupid and typical space laser, but who cares, he’s fighting a DUCK. Watch if you want to have fun!
Neil Breen is a genius. This movie is like trying to follow a 5 years old logic. 10/10 no notes. Actually two notes, not enough laptops and not enough books thrown.

This movie is very strange, and honestly feels like a movie of 2 halves, with the second half (leaving the hotel) being more interesting than the first. The stilted dialogue and scenic grey-ish shots feel like Wes Anderson, but evil. I think conceptually, it’s interesting, and the acting is good, in that everyone plays like this awkward/unemotionalness well and it’s weird and unsettling, but it takes a long time to get used to. I feel like there’s way too much background that you have to slowly learn and it kind of makes it confusing for a while. This movie is definitely an acquired taste. 5.5/10

I think this is stylistically the best looking Spiderman movie. The suit really stands out. I think the fight scenes are really good. I also think the story is interesting, dealing with themes of isolation, burning yourself out, and identity. Everyone likes a sad Spiderman. It just felt like it was missing the BIG fight, though the Hulk/Punisher one was good, though short.

7.5/10

The shit is freaky. Credit to Inde Navarrete because she absolutely killed it. Easily switching between moods and her freaky movements. The movie does a great job of this underlying sense of dread and fear. The lighting and framing  I also noticed is top notch, with just glimpses of Nikki in corners or obscuring her face. I’m not one for horror, but this was excited so well. 8.5/10

This movie is very intriguing to watch. The set design, dialogue, acting and most scene are very gripping and compelling. It’s a bit hard to follow the goal of the journey (making it through the woods?). The crucifixion procession is kind of eerie to watch in a hard to look away way. The portrayal of death is really intriguing, almost like he’s just doing a job, and I like that he’s completely separate from God and Satan. The movie is also surprisingly funny, with the squire being particularly funny. The end scene of the death march is very creepy in the framing and movement. This is a movie that will take a bit to grab you, but once it does, you’re locked in. 9/10

Classic fun action hijinks. The plots pretty simple, but it’s fun. Sean Connery and Nicholas Cage are both entertaining, especially with the one liners. The rocket man line is great. I actually like the layer of the main bad guy not wanting to kill and having not pure evil motives, it added a fun twist. 7/10

This is a great movie. Dominic Sessa does a great job playing a young Anthony Bourdain who is scared, angry, ambitious, dumbly in love. I think he’s great at switching emotions in a dime. Antonio Banderas chef character is intriguing and you want to learn more about him. It’s genuinely funny with a lot of laughs, but some really good emotion. “I want you to take the picture, because I like the way I feel when you look at me” 🧑‍🍳😘. I really love the use of sound and lack of, making scenes frenetic, or tense, or upbeat, etc. I also like the mirroring of the start to the end. 8.5/10

The original cast have the same charm and connection as the first one. The mummy may return, but the terrible CGI returns too. I feel like the jokes were less funny than the original, and the kid is really annoying to me. But it’s a fun 2 hour adventure movie, with a fun cast.

This may be the trippiest movie I’ve ever watched, and certainly one of the most uncomfortable. I’m not really one for thrillers, but this one had me gripped. The movie does a very good job of blending each scene into the next, so you really have no idea what is real and what is delusion, and it makes it genuinely uncomfortable. I think also the story of Mima wanting to be an actress, but being uncomfortable with the exploitation, but doing it to appease others, while in combination with being supportive her ex-band mates for an interesting dynamic, and keeps you on your toes. The ending is genuinely surprising! Also, the voice actress for Mima was amazing, genuinely hard to watch sometimes because of her performance. It does get a little too hard to track at the end, and you might wanna go to Reddit after to make sure you got it. 8.5/10

A very cool movie, with a world, score and visual that really engross you. The plot is very interesting, though at times hard to fully keep up with, with a lot of dots needing to be connected. The end scene with the body growing was really gross to watch. I think the message of humans messing with powers they shouldn’t, especially when tied to bombing/japan leads to a very strong message that doesn’t slap you in the face, but you realize throughout, and makes you more appreciative 7.5/10

There’s something about this movie, whether it be the sound, pacing, colors, or something else that makes it really comfortable. Like you feel at home with the characters. As a Scarlett Johansson hater, I have to say this was a really good performance, subdued, whimsical and confused. And bill murray does a very good job at playing jaded. That being said, the relationship dynamic, especially with the age difference + marriage makes it a bit awkward. I can understand the lost souls thing, but it’s a bit hard to justify. The movie itself is cozy, just not a fan of that part. 7/10

This is a beautiful movie, with a near perfect performance by Kirk Douglas as Van Gogh. He is able to switch between misery, paranoia, anger, joy so seamlessly. The story is very interesting and very well paced, with most of it being quite engrossing (there’s maybe about 10-15 mins in the middle that are a bit boring, but that’s not too big a deal). The soundtrack and use of color are also great, adding depth and tension to each scene. This really feels like an epic, but more human and personal. 9/10

viewings.film: the life aquatic with steve zissou|2004
viewings.review: I would describe this movie as a grower. Unlike fantastic Mr. Fox and Grand Budapest Hotel, this one takes a little time to get truly invested in. But I think around the 30 minute mark, it really starts to get engaging. I think there’s a lot of good dry humor mixed with some good character relations. I really enjoyed Willem Dafoe in particular. I really like the scene of them stealing the stuff from Jeff Goldblum’s lab and the father son talk between Zizou and Ned when they’re moving around the cabin. The death was also very surprising! I also think that the action scene at the the old hotel was pretty good definitely compared to the other two Wes Anderson films I’ve seen so far. It’s not my favourite, but I do think it’s interesting.

This is a movie with a very simple plot, but done very well. All of the performances are great, with all of the talents shining through tremendously. Gene Kelly is particularly charming and his number “I Got” with the kids was my favorite scene. I think Adam’s dry humor and straight man routine was really funny. I do feel bad for Henri though, he got the short end of the stick. 7.5/10

viewings.film: dr strangelove or how i learned to stop worrying and love the bomb|1964
viewings.review: A really funny movie! I think a lot of the jokes are really funny: the excessive gum chewing of Buck, the conversations between the president and Premier, Jacks rants in general, answering to the Coca Cola company. I also think all the performances and characters are top notch, especially George C Scott as Buck with his crazy facial expressions and Sterling Hayden as Ripper and his calm demeanor in the gun fights. I thought Strangelove was a bit confusing at first, but towards the end it became super funny of the suppressive Nazi. This movie holds up great and is really visually appealing too! 9.5/10

What an emotional film. You feel so many emotions, suspense to see John, fear when the people go into his room and antagonize him, and the sadness when he gets emotional when meeting Treves wife was poignant. The score in particular only adds on to these emotions. Jonathan Hurts performance was amazing. You can feel the pain. This is a beautiful story very well done. Maybe the most I’ve felt watching a movie in a long time. 9/10

Maybe a top 10 movie soundtrack of all time? The use of music in this movie is really top notch and helps to either add tension or levity well. George Clooney’s Ulysses’s refined vernacular compared to Pete and Delmar’s simple ones makes for an interesting dialogue. Also, this movie is fun for spotting the Odyssey references, but doesn’t punish you if you don’t know them. A fun film. 7.5/10

Sandman is a bad friend. This is a charming movie with a very simple plot. I think Paul giamattis acting is really good. Though the wine conversation between maya and miles is a bit on the nose, it’s probably my favorite part of the movie. It’s annoying that Jack gets little comeuppance, but I guess it just shows the difference between the 2. The ending feels a bit lame. 6/10

I think there are some really good performances in the movie. Sean penns performance is unhinged and his haircut is nuts. Leo’s is fun and neurotic. The plot and world building is interesting. I don’t think there’s any particular stand out moments in the film, but is fun to watch. The music underlying in each scene also really helps to add to either tension or emotional weight. 7/10

This feels like the opposite of Seventh Seal, and in a great way. The movie feels very personal and up close, with Victor Sjörstörms performance really being the driving force. His small mannerisms and expressions really sell the idea of a man who’s coming face to face with mortality. The themes of time and mortality really are woven in and explored well, with the handless clocks being my favorite motif. Also, the dream sequences are well made, with my first being my favorite, with the brightness really adding to it. This is so close to seventh seal, and I really enjoy the simple end. 9/10

A very interesting plot. Not much of a sci fi enjoyer normally, but this plot was very intriguing, with a lot of political undertones that help make the story more engaging. This is what Don’t Look Up wanted to be. Robert Pattinson, as usual, does a top notch job. His performance as Mickey 17 and 18 are quite separate enough that it makes both performances enjoyable. I do wish we saw other mickeys having different personalities, as they all appear the same roughly. I also feel like the movies a bit long personally, but not too long. Also, it looks very good, like visually impressive and great quality. 8/10

Obviously very good. Peter O’Tooles performance was amazing, probably a top 10. And the character is very interesting, as you slowly watch him lose it (or I guess let the veil slip depending on your interpretation). The cinematography (with the camera work and transitions) were top notch. A lot of far shots to help build the scale and or suspense. I also think the scale of the desert was really well done. It really made the journey feel epic. I also think that the use of music was really interesting, where it’s primarily used for happy triumphant moments, and the sadder or tense ones are more silent, so you sit with the weight more. I also think the deaths throughout feel very weighted and shift his character more and more (with Hasims being very shocking considering the triumph of his rescue). The length is my only gripe id say. There are times where it goes really fast (particularly the second hour I would say), but there are times where I feel like it crawls a bit, moreso the last 40 minutes I’d say. This is still an amazing movie with amazing character work, cinematography, score, and acting. 9.5/10.

This movie is grungy, confusing, and has a lot of shitty people getting very little comeuppance. All things that usually make me dislike a movie. That being said, I really like this movie. I think this movies biggest strength is its pacing, where there’s not a second of scene that feels like filler or slow. Even though I knew the twist going in (my fault for not seeing it sooner), seeing it play out was still quite rewarding and still intriguing. Edward Norton does a very good job switching between pathetic to “confident” and Brad Pitt plays cool very well, surprising… The ending is a tad confusing with the gunshot, but then again so is the whole movie. Once he figures it out and is working against himself in particular I’d say I like the most. Though there are plenty of good scenes throughout, especially the driving scene. Also, a top tier needle drop at the end. 8.5/10

Very silly and stupid, but in a fun way. The first half has some good jokes, but is a bit forgettable. The second half, once they get to the musical, is very funny. The whole “Springtime for Hitler” show is ridiculously funny. I love the ex-Nazi character, he’s the funniest part of the movie. 7.5/10

A beautiful movie with some amazing connections. The connections between the sisters and their connections with their father are all really well explored, though I wish there was bit more depth to the youngest sister. Still, the dynamics between characters is amazing and makes the movie very compelling. And the way food is used is so interesting. It’s this labor of love for Chu, as you seen the time and effort he puts in, yet almost every single time there’s food in a scene, it involves a fight, death or the family being split up, almost like an omen. The one who appreciates his food the most Shan-Shan, he develops a care for and wants to keep impressing her, as if he’s filling the void for his lack of daughters’ affection. And his taste almost mirroring his love/passion, losing it slowly, and in the end he can regain it and the connection with his daughter. And Jia-Chien looks the most happy when she’s cooking, as if the cycle continues. Also some of the best food I’ve seen in a movie. Emotional and feel-good 8.5/10

Pretty decent movie. I think some of the story beats are a bit predictable. I think they do a really good job of building tension in scenes, particularly the jail scene with Bob and Little Bill. Gene Hackmans performance was probably my favorite, he goes between fun and threatening pretty well. I also like that he’s pressured to drink throughout the film, and they make note of it, and when he finally takes the drink it’s actually pretty subtle and you almost miss it. The ending is probably the highlight. 7.5/10
